Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for Folly, Facebook's Open-source Library.

<explanation>
To create an accurate system design diagram for Folly, follow these guidelines:

1. High-Level Architecture Components
   
   Draw the main components as distinct sections:

   a. Core Library Components
   - Place at the center of the diagram
   - Include fundamental modules like Memory, Synchronization, Containers, etc.
   - Use rectangular boxes with rounded corners

   b. Supporting Infrastructure
   - Position around the core components
   - Include build systems, testing framework, and documentation
   - Use different shapes (e.g., hexagons) to distinguish from core components

2. Component Organization

   Create these major groupings:

   a. Foundation Layer (Bottom)
   - Portability (/folly/portability/)
   - Memory Management (/folly/memory/)
   - System Utilities (/folly/system/)

   b. Core Functionality Layer (Middle)
   - Synchronization primitives (/folly/synchronization/)
   - Containers (/folly/container/)
   - String utilities (/folly/String.h, /folly/FBString.h)
   - Futures & Promises (/folly/futures/)
   - Executors (/folly/executors/)

   c. Advanced Features Layer (Top)
   - Fiber system (/folly/fibers/)
   - Experimental features (/folly/experimental/)
   - Logging system (/folly/logging/)
   - IO utilities (/folly/io/)

3. Dependencies and Interactions

   Show relationships using different arrow types:
   - Solid arrows for direct dependencies
   - Dashed arrows for optional dependencies
   - Double-headed arrows for bidirectional interactions

4. External Dependencies

   Create a separate section showing integration with:
   - Boost
   - OpenSSL
   - Google Test
   - Format library
   - Other external libraries

5. Color Coding

   Use distinct colors to represent:
   - Blue: Core components
   - Green: Stable APIs
   - Yellow: Experimental features
   - Gray: External dependencies
   - Red: Critical system components

6. Special Considerations

   Highlight important aspects:
   - Performance-critical paths (bold lines)
   - Thread-safety boundaries (dotted containers)
   - Async/sync boundaries (dashed lines)
   - Memory management flows (green arrows)

7. Component Details

   For each major component, include:
   - Name
   - Key classes/features
   - Thread safety guarantees
   - Performance characteristics

8. Legend

   Create a comprehensive legend showing:
   - All shapes used
   - Arrow types and meanings
   - Color coding scheme
   - Special indicators
   - Version information

9. Notes Section

   Add a notes section indicating:
   - Platform support (Linux, Windows, macOS)
   - C++ version requirements (C++17)
   - Build system requirements
   - Performance considerations

10. Implementation Details

    For critical components, show:
    - Key algorithms used
    - Memory layout
    - Threading model
    - Error handling approach

The diagram should emphasize:
- The practical, performance-focused nature of the library
- The flat organizational structure
- The independence of components
- The extensive testing infrastructure
- The focus on modern C++ features

Remember to maintain a balance between detail and clarity, as Folly is a large library with many components. The diagram should be readable at both high-level overview and detailed component level views.

</explanation>
